questions.stem:
(a) Define marketing. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four functions of marketing. [8 marks]
(c) Explain the following utilities created by marketing, with an example of each: (i) time utility; (ii) place utility; (iii) possession utility. [6 marks]
(d) State two reasons why marketing is important to a developing economy such as Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the process of identifying, anticipating and satisfying customer needs profitably through exchange
2 marks: buying/assembling goods
2 marks: selling
2 marks: transportation and storage
2 marks: financing / risk bearing / grading and standardisation / market information
2 marks: time utility: goods available when needed, e.g. storing grains for the lean season
2 marks: place utility: goods available where needed, e.g. moving onions from Sokoto to Port Harcourt
2 marks: possession utility: transfer of ownership, e.g. selling a car on credit
2 marks: creates employment in distribution, transport and advertising
2 marks: stimulates production and economic growth / raises living standards / expands export earnings
questions.explanation: Marketing identifies and satisfies customer needs profitably. Functions include buying, selling, transport, storage, financing, risk bearing, grading and market information. It creates time, place and possession utility. In Nigeria it creates jobs, stimulates production, raises living standards and helps exports.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain each of the four elements of the marketing mix. [8 marks]
(b) Distinguish between the micro-environment and the macro-environment of marketing. [4 marks]
(c) Explain four macro-environmental factors that affect the marketing of a product in Nigeria. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: product: the goods or services offered, including design, quality, branding and packaging
2 marks: price: the amount charged, including discounts and credit terms
2 marks: place: channels and physical distribution that get goods to customers
2 marks: promotion: communication to inform and persuade, e.g. advertising and sales promotion
2 marks: micro-environment: forces close to the firm such as suppliers, customers, competitors and intermediaries
2 marks: macro-environment: wider forces affecting all firms, largely uncontrollable
2 marks: political/legal factors, e.g. import bans, regulations
2 marks: economic factors, e.g. inflation, exchange rates, income levels
2 marks: socio-cultural factors, e.g. tastes, religion, population
2 marks: technological / physical (natural) factors, e.g. Internet, climate
questions.explanation: The 4 Ps are product, price, place and promotion. The micro-environment covers the firm's immediate actors (suppliers, customers, competitors, intermediaries, publics); the macro-environment covers broad PESTLE forces. In Nigeria, policy changes, inflation and exchange rates, tastes and culture, and technology all shape marketing.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a product? [2 marks]
(b) Describe the four stages of the product life cycle, stating one marketing action suitable for each stage. [12 marks]
(c) State three functions of packaging. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: anything offered to a market to satisfy a want or need, including goods, services and ideas
2 marks: introduction: low sales, high costs, few competitors
1 mark: action: informative advertising / free samples
2 marks: growth: rapid sales growth, profits rise, competitors enter
1 mark: action: expand distribution / build brand preference
2 marks: maturity: sales peak and level off, intense competition
1 mark: action: modify product / promotions / reduce price
2 marks: decline: sales and profits fall
1 mark: action: cut costs, withdraw or rejuvenate the product
2 marks: protects the product from damage and contamination
2 marks: promotes the product through attractive design and branding
2 marks: provides information / convenience in handling and use
questions.explanation: A product is anything offered to satisfy a need. Introduction (slow sales; inform and sample), growth (rising sales and competitors; widen distribution), maturity (peak sales and fierce competition; modify, promote, adjust price), decline (falling sales; cut costs or withdraw). Packaging protects, promotes, informs and makes handling convenient.

questions.stem:
(a) Define market segmentation. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four bases for segmenting a consumer market, with an example of each. [12 marks]
(c) State three benefits of market segmentation to a firm. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: dividing a total market into distinct groups of buyers with similar needs or characteristics
3 marks: geographic: by region, state, urban/rural, e.g. heavier wrappers for the cold Plateau area
3 marks: demographic: by age, sex, income, e.g. toys for children
3 marks: psychographic: by lifestyle, personality, social class, e.g. premium goods for high earners
3 marks: behavioural: by usage rate, benefits sought, loyalty, e.g. bulk packs for heavy users
2 marks: better understanding of customer needs
2 marks: more efficient use of marketing resources
2 marks: helps identify market opportunities / increases sales and loyalty
questions.explanation: Segmentation divides a market into groups with similar needs. Bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic and behavioural. Benefits include better understanding of customers, efficient use of resources, identification of opportunities, tailored marketing mixes and stronger loyalty.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the five stages of the consumer buying decision process. [10 marks]
(b) Explain four factors that influence consumer buying behaviour. [8 marks]
(c) State one difference between consumer buying and organisational buying. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: need recognition: the consumer becomes aware of a need
2 marks: information search: seeks information from personal, commercial and public sources
2 marks: evaluation of alternatives: compares brands on attributes and price
2 marks: purchase decision: chooses and buys
2 marks: post-purchase behaviour: satisfaction or dissonance, affecting repeat purchase
2 marks: cultural factors, e.g. culture, sub-culture, social class
2 marks: social factors, e.g. family, reference groups, roles
2 marks: personal factors, e.g. age, occupation, income, lifestyle
2 marks: psychological factors, e.g. motivation, perception, learning, attitudes
2 marks: organisational buying involves larger quantities, more people and more formal procedures than consumer buying
questions.explanation: The process runs from need recognition through information search, evaluation, purchase and post-purchase behaviour. Cultural, social, personal and psychological factors influence buying. Organisational buying is more formal, in larger quantities, rational and involves a buying centre.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four pricing strategies a manufacturer may adopt. [8 marks]
(b) State four factors that influence the price of a product. [4 marks]
(c) A manufacturer of school bags has fixed costs of N900,000. Each bag costs N2,500 in variable costs and sells for N4,000. Calculate (i) the contribution per bag; (ii) the break-even quantity; (iii) the profit if 1,000 bags are sold. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: penetration pricing: low initial price to win market share
2 marks: skimming: high initial price for new/innovative products, lowered later
2 marks: cost-plus pricing: cost plus a mark-up
2 marks: psychological / prestige / discount / going-rate pricing explained
1 mark: cost of production
1 mark: demand and customers' ability to pay
1 mark: competition
1 mark: government policy / objectives of the firm / stage in life cycle
2 marks: contribution = 4,000 - 2,500 = N1,500
3 marks: break-even = 900,000 / 1,500 = 600 bags
3 marks: profit = 1,000 x 1,500 - 900,000 = N600,000
questions.explanation: Strategies include penetration, skimming, cost-plus, psychological, prestige and going-rate pricing. Price depends on costs, demand, competition, government policy and objectives. Contribution per bag is N1,500; break-even is 600 bags; selling 1,000 bags gives 1,500,000 - 900,000 = N600,000 profit.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between advertising and sales promotion. [4 marks]
(b) Explain four types of advertising. [8 marks]
(c) State four advantages and four disadvantages of television as an advertising medium. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: advertising is paid non-personal communication by an identified sponsor through mass media
2 marks: sales promotion uses short-term incentives such as coupons, samples and discounts to stimulate immediate buying
2 marks: informative advertising: tells the market about a new product
2 marks: persuasive/competitive advertising: urges buyers to choose a brand over rivals
2 marks: reminder advertising: keeps the product in the minds of buyers
2 marks: institutional / generic / corrective advertising explained
1 mark: advantage: combines sight, sound and motion
1 mark: advantage: reaches a large audience
1 mark: advantage: can demonstrate the product
1 mark: advantage: high impact and prestige
1 mark: disadvantage: very expensive
1 mark: disadvantage: short life of the message
1 mark: disadvantage: power failures limit viewing
1 mark: disadvantage: does not reach people without televisions / clutter of advertisements
questions.explanation: Advertising is paid mass-media communication; sales promotion offers short-term incentives. Types include informative, persuasive, reminder, institutional, generic and corrective advertising. Television offers sight, sound, motion, wide reach and demonstration but is costly, short-lived, affected by power outages and misses those without sets.

questions.stem:
(a) Draw up, in words, three channels of distribution for consumer goods, showing the intermediaries in each. [6 marks]
(b) Explain four functions of the wholesaler to the manufacturer. [8 marks]
(c) Explain three factors that determine the choice of a channel of distribution. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: producer to consumer (direct)
2 marks: producer to retailer to consumer
2 marks: producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer (or with agent)
2 marks: buys in bulk, relieving the manufacturer of storage problems
2 marks: provides finance by paying promptly / reduces manufacturer's distribution costs
2 marks: bears risk of price changes and deterioration
2 marks: gives market information / promotes and distributes to retailers
2 marks: nature of the product, e.g. perishable or technical
2 marks: nature and location of the market / number of customers
2 marks: cost of the channel / financial strength of the producer / control desired / competitors' channels
questions.explanation: Channels: producer-consumer; producer-retailer-consumer; producer-wholesaler-retailer-consumer (agents may be added). Wholesalers buy in bulk, store, finance, bear risks, distribute and supply market information. Channel choice depends on the product, market, costs, control and the producer's resources.

questions.stem:
(a) Define international marketing. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four methods by which a Nigerian firm may enter a foreign market. [8 marks]
(c) Explain five problems facing Nigerian exporters. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the marketing of goods and services across national borders
2 marks: direct exporting: the firm sells directly to foreign buyers
2 marks: indirect exporting: through export agents or trading houses
2 marks: licensing / franchising: allowing a foreign firm to use its brand or process for a fee
2 marks: joint venture or wholly owned subsidiary abroad
2 marks: poor quality and standards of some products
2 marks: inadequate infrastructure and high transport costs
2 marks: exchange-rate instability and finance problems
2 marks: stiff foreign competition and trade barriers
2 marks: bureaucratic export procedures / poor information on foreign markets / cultural differences
questions.explanation: International marketing is marketing across borders. Entry methods include direct and indirect exporting, licensing, franchising, joint ventures and subsidiaries. Exporters face quality and standards issues, poor infrastructure, finance and exchange-rate problems, competition, trade barriers, cumbersome procedures and limited market information.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term e-marketing. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four ways in which a business can use ICT in marketing. [8 marks]
(c) State five advantages of online marketing over traditional marketing. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the use of the Internet and other digital technologies to promote and sell goods and services
2 marks: websites/online stores for e-commerce
2 marks: social media marketing on platforms such as Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp
2 marks: e-mail and SMS marketing
2 marks: customer databases, online payments, online research or search-engine advertising
2 marks: reaches a wider (even global) audience
2 marks: lower cost than many traditional media
2 marks: available 24 hours a day
2 marks: allows targeting and personalised messages
2 marks: results can be measured easily / quick feedback from customers
questions.explanation: E-marketing uses digital technologies to market goods. Firms use websites, social media, e-mail/SMS, search advertising, databases and online payments. Online marketing reaches more people at lower cost, runs round the clock, targets customers precisely and gives measurable, rapid feedback.
